title: Johor coach says foreign players may start entire lineup against Jeonbuk
text:
Johor coach says foreign players may start entire lineup against Jeonbuk - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 3일(화) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Johor coach says foreign players may start entire lineup against Jeonbuk 
 입력 2026.11.03. 11:40 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 A Malaysian pro team but could it have no Malaysian players in the best 11?
 Jeonbuk will face Johor Darul Ta'zim FC in the AFC Champions League Elite League phase 4 round at Jeonju World Cup Stadium on the 3rd. Johor, a prestigious club representing Malaysia, is unbeaten in 2 wins and 1 draw, including a 2-0 win over Pohang, and sits fourth. Jeonbuk (1-1-1) is down in 10th place.
 An official press conference was held at Jeonju World Cup Stadium on the 2nd, a day before the decisive match. Francisco Muñoz, Johor's coach, and Oscar Arribas attended the press conference.
 Coach Muñoz said, "The most important thing in the match is to attack and continue our momentum. Tomorrow will be a difficult match. The opponent Jeonbuk is strong. Their defense is good and their midfield is good. It will be a difficult match tomorrow, but we want to win," he said.
 Johor, a prestigious Malaysian team, has a unique player composition. From coach Cisco, he is Spanish. In addition, there are as many as 12 players from Brazil and Spain. The other players form a multinational squad from Iran, Portugal, Croatia, Argentina, Australia and others. There are 19 native Malaysian players.
 Even in the recent match against Pohang, only two Malaysian players were among Johor's best 11. One of them was the goalkeeper. If judged only by ability, Malaysian players could all be left out of the starting 11 against Jeonbuk, being outperformed by foreign players.
 When asked about the best 11 composition, Francisco Muñoz, Johor's coach, said, "That could happen," and said it is possible to field a best 11 made up only of foreign players.
 He said, "The most important thing is our team's organization. This is the stage where the best players in Asia play. Our team has Brazilian players and Spanish players. There are many good players. They have good speed and a fast tempo. There are many skilled players," and he declared he would actively use foreign players.
 Muñoz added, "Football is wide open. You never know what will happen. Tomorrow, regardless of nationality, we will make the best choice for our team," he predicted.
 In the end, Jeonbuk must stop the offensive of the Brazilian and Spanish wingers. Spanish-born Arribas said, "Tomorrow we will try to play our football. Our fans came all the way to Korea. We prepared for the match humbly," pledging to win against Jeonbuk.
 [OSEN]
